title: Terms of use | Truffe
description: The plain-language terms for using Truffe, the pet health records app: not veterinary advice, check scans against the original, and your rights as a consumer.
body:
Terms of use

Truffe for iPhone · Effective {{UPDATED}}

The short version
  • Truffe keeps records and reminders. It is not veterinary advice.
  • Scans can misread a paper, so check what you save, especially dates and doses.
  • Your records are yours, and nothing here limits your rights as a consumer.

Who these terms are with

These terms are between you and Rayn Rosnuk, who makes apps as Loon Softworks (Ontario, Canada). If you download Truffe from the App Store, Apple’s standard End User License Agreement also applies. If the two conflict, Apple’s agreement wins for anything it covers.

Not veterinary advice

Truffe organizes information you give it and reminds you about dates. It does not diagnose, treat or recommend care. Always follow your veterinarian’s guidance. In an emergency, call your vet or the nearest emergency animal hospital; do not rely on the app.

Check what the scanner reads

Truffe reads printed and handwritten papers on your phone. It can misread a word, a date or a number, and it asks when a date could mean two things. You are responsible for checking each field before saving, and for confirming important dates, vaccines and doses against the original paper or with your vet.

Reminders

Reminders depend on your phone, its notification settings, battery and the dates you entered. A missed or late notification is possible. Treat reminders as a helpful backup, not the only way you track your pet’s care.

Local information

Licence rules, emergency numbers and similar local notes are provided for convenience, may be incomplete or out of date, and are not legal advice. Check with your city or local authority.

Your content

Records, photos and documents you add belong to you and stay on your device. You can export them at any time. Only add documents you have the right to keep.

Purchases

Truffe is free to download and free to use for one pet; the free version reads up to 5 scanned papers, and typing records in is always free. Truffe Plus, an optional purchase, adds unlimited pets, unlimited scans and the vaccine card PDF. It is offered as an auto-renewing subscription, monthly or yearly (the yearly plan may start with a free trial), or as a one-time lifetime purchase. The price in your currency and the renewal period are shown before you buy, and payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm. A subscription renews automatically at the same price unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period; you can manage or cancel it at any time in your Apple Account settings, and if you cancel during a free trial you are not charged. Payments, renewals and refunds are handled by Apple (or Google on Android) under their terms. Where the law gives you a refund right, request it from Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com. The app reminds you a few days before a free trial ends and about a month before a yearly subscription renews. If Truffe Plus ends, nothing you added is locked or deleted: every pet and record stays readable and exportable.

Acceptable use

Don’t reverse engineer, resell or misuse the app, or use it to break the law.

Liability

To the extent the law allows, Truffe is provided as is, and we are not liable for losses that come from relying on scanned data, missed reminders or local information. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under the consumer protection laws where you live, including Quebec’s Consumer Protection Act, or excludes liability that cannot legally be excluded.

Changes and law

If these terms change in a way that matters, we will update this page and the date above, and tell you in the app. These terms are governed by the laws of Ontario and Canada, except where the law where you live gives you the right to rely on it.
